💡 Key Takeaways

  • This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.
  • Industry observers note that the Coach Collection brings nine new items to The Sims 4.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Sims 4’s first enhancement of the year is here, though it may not be quite what you might have expected. The game’s latest patch mainly centres around a collaboration with Coach, the luxury fashion brand.

This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.

Industry observers note that the Coach Collection brings nine new items to The Sims 4. They range from clothes and accessories you can use with Create a Sim, to decoration items available in Build Buy. There’s also The Carriage House, a new Gallery household where you can find three new roommates.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a nice bit of variety in the options available, some casual and others more practical for your Sims to wear. Then there’s The Bag Room, which can also be grabbed from the Gallery. The room simply serves as a way for you to show off your Coach bags and trunks collection.

According to recent reports, in case you missed it, The Sims’ development team recently shared an update on some of what we can expect in 2026, both for The Sims 4 as well as other projects right now in the works. It even included further confirmation, if any was needed, that Project Rene is a dedicated mobile off-shoot, and not — as many had long believed — The Sims 5.

The blog post also included a statement about EA’s imminent change of ownership, which many fear could alter the series’ inclusive and diverse nature, and the decisions made by its various teams.

#156586. AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1337 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1337 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed.
  • Industry observers note that for years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works.
  • But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A newly introduced study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.

Industry observers note that for years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.

But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

"Artificial intelligence systems are often described as 'brain-like' because they can predict activity in parts of the brain that help us recognize objects," says York University Assistant Professor Kohitij Kar, senior author of a latest study. "Until now, scientists mostly tested this in one direction. They asked whether AI models can predict brain activity.".

A New Test Reveals a Hidden Problem With Brain-Like AI.

The York University team decided to approach this question from the opposite direction. Rather than simply measuring how well AI could predict the activity of brain cells, they investigated whether recorded brain activity could also predict what was happening inside the AI models.

It has been revealed that if these systems truly operate like the brain, the researchers reasoned, the relationship should work in both directions. To investigate, they developed a method called reverse predictivity testing, which allowed them to evaluate similarities that conventional tests could overlook.

According to recent reports, "Ultimately, we need computational models to truly understand the underlying neural mechanisms of how we recognize objects. How do we see objects move? While it's a very easy task that we do every day, computationally, though, it's a very challenging problem," claims Kar, the Canada Research Chair in Visual Neuroscience and a member of York's Centre for Vision Research and Centre for Integrative and Applied Neuroscience.

The research team, which included York Postdoctoral Fellow Sabine Muzellec, a trainee with the university's Connected Minds program, examined responses to a wide variety of visual images.

Industry observers note that their tests included 1,320 natural photographs and realistic synthetic images featuring 10 familiar subjects: a bear, an elephant, a face, an apple, a car, a dog, a chair, a plane, a bird, and a zebra. These objects appeared against a variety of natural scenes and indoor or outdoor backgrounds. The researchers also introduced 300 additional images showing the same subjects in different visual styles, including outlines, drawings, simplified representations, and artistic interpretations.

AI Can Predict Brain Activity, but the Reverse Tells a Different Story.

The results revealed a significant disconnect between artificial intelligence and biological vision.

It has been revealed that AI models were generally successful at predicting the responses of recorded neurons, which are the specialized cells that transmit information throughout the brain. However, when the researchers reversed the process, those same neuronal responses were much less effective at predicting many of the models' internal features.

This difference was particularly revealing because the researchers did not observe the same problem when comparing neuronal activity across different brains.

Recent findings suggest that "The results were striking. While AI models can predict the neurons we recorded in the brain fairly well, the brain cannot equally predict many of the model's internal features. Interestingly, this is not the case when neurons from one brain is compared against ones from another brain," notes Kar.

The findings suggest that an AI system can produce results that closely resemble those of the brain while relying on very different internal mechanisms. In other words, matching the brain's responses does not necessarily mean that the underlying processes are the same.

Sources indicate that kar warns that this distinction could become increasingly important as artificial intelligence advances. If researchers continue refining models based only on how accurately they predict neural activity, differences between those models and actual primate brains could accumulate over time.

That would undermine one of the main reasons neuroscientists use these systems in the first place: to develop realistic explanations of how the brain works.

"The findings suggest that today's AI systems solve visual tasks partly using internal strategies that the brain may not use. Importantly, the parts of AI models that align with the brain are also better at predicting real human behavior," notes Kar.

Why the Discovery Matters for Neuroscience and Human Behavior.

Recent findings suggest that the implications extend well beyond computer vision. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to help researchers design experiments, study human behavior, and investigate neurological and psychological conditions. Many of these applications depend on the assumption that AI models process information in ways that resemble the human brain.

If that assumption is incorrect, researchers could draw misleading conclusions from models that appear accurate on the surface but operate differently underneath.

"Our findings challenge how similar current AI systems really are with the primate brain. We show that models that were previously thought to be brain-like rely on internal components that the brain does not appear to use. We provide a well-vetted diagnostic metric for the field," says Muzellec.

According to recent reports, developing AI systems that more faithfully reproduce brain function could eventually improve research into conditions ranging from post-traumatic stress disorder to autism. For now, however, the newly identified differences highlight the need for caution when using existing models to investigate human behavior or guide clinical research.

The concern may also apply to other areas of neuroscience. Similar artificial intelligence models are already being used to study hearing, language, and movement. If those systems also rely on internal processes that differ from biological ones, researchers may need to reconsider how much they can reveal about the nervous system.

Building AI That More Closely Matches the Human Brain.

Rather than suggesting that artificial neural networks should be abandoned, the findings provide a way to make them more useful and scientifically reliable.

By identifying which features of an AI model correspond to real neural activity, researchers can focus on developing systems that more accurately reflect the biological mechanisms behind perception.

In a recent development, "Our approach helps identify which parts of an ANN truly match brain activity, allowing us to build more reliable models for understanding how people see and interpret the world," says Kar. "This is especially key for our autism research program, which builds on models of the neurotypical brain as a baseline.".

It has been revealed that A neurotypical brain refers to one with patterns of neurological development and functioning generally considered typical. Establishing accurate models of these patterns is key for researchers investigating how perception and information processing may differ in conditions such as autism.

To help other scientists put their findings into practice, the team has released a publicly available testing toolkit that AI developers can use to evaluate their own models and identify opportunities for improvement.

Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, the study introduces a new approach to evaluating artificial intelligence that goes beyond measuring how well a system performs a task. The researchers argue that understanding whether AI reaches its results through processes that genuinely resemble those of the brain is just as crucial.

The discovery could help guide the development of a fresh generation of AI models that not only recognize the world with impressive accuracy, but also offer a more faithful picture of how the human brain makes sense of what it sees.

Materials provided by York University. Original written by Sandra McLean. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Review: Volvo’s 2028 XC60/90 PHEVs get 80 miles of EV range, changing the game

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volvo flew us out to Copenhagen to drive across the bridge to Sweden to check out the upcoming 2028 XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids.
  • At Electrek, we’re usually pretty skeptical of plug-in hybrids.
  • Volvo’s upcoming 2028 XC60 T8 and XC90 T8 “Long-Range” PHEVs are the rare exception that actually force us to pay attention.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volvo flew us out to Copenhagen to drive across the bridge to Sweden to check out the upcoming 2028 XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids. The fresh vehicles promise to double the EV-only range to 73-78 miles, making them a new breed of hybrid rarely seen outside China. But what can you do with so much EV-only range?

At Electrek, we’re usually pretty skeptical of plug-in hybrids. Too many are glorified gas cars with 20-mile batteries that owners often don’t bother to charge. The electric-only powertrain is often underpowered and not something you can actually use day-to-day.

Volvo’s upcoming 2028 XC60 T8 and XC90 T8 “Long-Range” PHEVs are the rare exception that actually force us to pay attention. By stuffing a 41.2 kWh floor-mounted battery (37.9 kWh usable) into its solid but aging SPA1 platform, Volvo has more than doubled the electric range of its two bestselling SUVs. Both now have more battery capacity and range than the original all-electric Nissan Leaf, Hyundai Ioniq, and many of the compliance EVs that followed. Volvo also doubled the charging speed from 3.6kW to a more reasonable 7.2 kW, meaning charge times are roughly unchanged.

Industry observers note that both the XC60 and XC90 share the exact same T8 AWD hardware: a 247-hp 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder up front with a 70-hp front e-boost motor, and an upgraded 174-hp electric motor on the rear axle. Combined output lands at a healthy 455 horsepower and 560 lb-ft of torque.

The real headline, though, is the electric range:.

Those numbers easily crown both Volvos as the longest-range plug-in hybrids coming to the U.S. market, blowing past the Mercedes-Benz GLE 450e, Toyota RAV4 Prime, and Range Rover PHEVs, which top out around 50 miles. With the average American commuting around 30 to 40 miles a day, you can genuinely treat either of these SUVs like a full EV Monday through Friday without waking up the gas engine once…or so it would appear on paper.

According to recent reports, sadly, there are some caveats to consider that will make these a little harder to run EV-only. First, to accelerate swiftly off the line or to operate in AWD mode, the gas engine needs to engage. That makes winter driving and spirited driving a gas-usage endeavor. Also, without DC fast charging, the Level 2 charger tops out at 7.2 kW, meaning longer trips will also require gas usage.

On the plus side, even with the cold weather and snow tires, I saw range over 145 kilometers/90 miles on the XC60 when fully charged.

If you don’t need a third row, the XC60 is easily the more compelling package.

It has been revealed that at 4,855 lbs, it’s quick—ripping from 0–60 mph in 4.5 seconds—and surprisingly efficient for a bulky crossover, sipping 48 kWh per 100 miles in electric mode and returning 29 mpg combined once the battery is depleted. Unlike the XC90, the 2028 XC60 also gets a proper visual refresh, complete with a cleaner front fascia, Matrix LED headlights, horizontal taillights, and an updated interior featuring Google Gemini on its not huge but very usable 11.2-inch touchscreen.

According to recent reports, it’s also the easier daily driver in tight spaces, with a 37.4-foot turning circle and slightly more first- and second-row legroom than its bigger sibling. The trade-off is utility: you’re limited to 21.1 cu. ft. of cargo space behind the second row and a 3,500-lb towing capacity.

The XC90 is the family hauler for buyers who want a three-row electric SUV but aren’t quite ready to jump into an EX90 or Rivian R1S.

According to recent reports, because Volvo redesigned the battery into a flat, floor-mounted pack, you don’t lose the XC90’s practicality. You still get 6- or 7-passenger seating, 34.5 cu. ft. of cargo room behind the second row (up to 69.4 cu. ft. max), and a serious 5,000-lb towing rating. Even with the extra bulk, it hits 60 mph in 4.9 seconds.

Industry observers note that the downside? Efficiency drops to 53 kWh per 100 miles (27 mpg on gas), the third row’s 31.9 inches of legroom is still best reserved for kids, and outside of the newly introduced battery and Google Gemini integration, the cabin and exterior are essentially carryovers, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing since we love Volvo interiors.

There are plenty of decently-long-range PHEVs available in Europe comparable to these things (e.g. VWAG's ones); it isn't only China. Also, a lot of them are far more affordable (and thus a reasonable alternative for people looking to save on motoring costs).

Availability isn't the problem so much as finding anyone who is interested in both owning and plugging in a PHEV. Almost anyone who is serious about minimising fuel use just gets a BEV instead.

Even with a 41.2 kWh pack, you can’t completely hide the compromises of a plug-in hybrid:.

Look, we’d still rather see buyers go all-electric with the upcoming EX60 or EX90, and if Volvo prices these 2028 T8s too close to $70,000–$80,000 when deliveries start in early 2027, going full BEV will still be a no-brainer in my book.

Sources indicate that but for those who aren’t ready to make the leap to full EV, these vehicles are incredibly compelling. Every morning, assuming you’re on a Level 2 charger, you have almost 80 miles of EV range, about double the average American daily usage. Then, of course, the backup of the 18-gallon tank and gas motor for those edge cases like trips or towing in cold weather are covered.

Recent findings suggest that so the takeaway: if you’re going to build a plug-in hybrid in 2027, this is how you do it. Giving drivers 73 to 78 miles of real electric range turns the gas engine from a daily necessity into a road-trip range extender. For households with a Level 2 home charger that still have lingering charging anxiety on long highway trips, the 2028 XC60 and XC90 T8 are easily the smartest PHEVs on the market. Not to mention the smooth, quick and safe rides Volvo is known for.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that would you wait a decade for a new car?
  • According to recent reports, delays were reportedly caused by the failure to secure funding to build a factory in Wales among other crises.
  • Industry observers note that there isn’t room for any detailed history of TVR here, but the original incarnation of the sport car maker collapsed into bankruptcy in 2006, having become both famous and infamous for brutish, fiber-bodied models including the 1990 Griffith, 1996 Cerbera and 1999 Tuscan Speed Six.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that would you wait a decade for a new car? That’s the situation for anybody who raised their hand to buy the TVR Griffith when it was declared as far back as 2017. R&T’s own interest in the story faded soon after the reborn British brand announced the car was going to be heavily delayed. But, in truth, nobody realized how long the wait would be.

According to recent reports, delays were reportedly caused by the failure to secure funding to build a factory in Wales among other crises. It’s fair to say that the interest of most onlookers, and surely all of the potential buyers , faded as the excuses piled up. But after a change in ownership last year, TVR's latest parent MOTV Group has revealed that the Griffith will be produced at the Lotus factory in Hethel, with the first customer deliveries “planned for 2028,” although those likely restricted to buyers in the U.K.

Industry observers note that there isn’t room for any detailed history of TVR here, but the original incarnation of the sport car maker collapsed into bankruptcy in 2006, having become both famous and infamous for brutish, fiber-bodied models including the 1990 Griffith, 1996 Cerbera and 1999 Tuscan Speed Six. Also the semi-mythical, one-of-one Speed 12 which was a star of early Gran Turismo games. TVR was reborn in 2013 after software entrepreneur Les Edgar bought the rights to the brand; according to public records in the U.K., Edgar resigned from the tech giant board earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that MOTV Group was previously known as Charge Holdings, with subsidiary Charge Cars planning to build an electrified restomod version of the 1967 Ford Mustang before it, too, collapsed into bankruptcy. In 2025, Charge was saved by a group of investors and subsequently merged with TVR.

According to recent reports, the official announcement of TVR’s latest return was accompanied by an image of what appears to be the 2017 concept car, now wrapped in a new disguise. Comparison of the images shows the same headlight position, panel lines, side-exit exhaust and identically patterned wheels. MOTV states the car will have a spaceframe chassis, a composite body, a V-8 engine with a manual transmission, and rear-wheel drive - all details aligning the 2017 version.

According to recent reports, the original blueprint was for the latest Griffith to use the iStream production process created by Gordon Murray’s then technology company, but this subsidiary has since been sold to ForSeven, which subsequently acquired McLaren Automotive which presumably owns the rights. So It will be interesting to discover if this technology-sharing partnership remains in place. Similarly, there is no confirmation that Cosworth is still involved in fettling the Ford Coyote V-8 that was meant to power the car as was originally revealed.

Beyond the above facts the official announcement was short on details beyond naming the senior executive team, these including CEO Paul Abercrombie and CTO Steve MacManus, who was formerly an engineering vice president at Tesla and who seems to have worked on the aborted Apple car project.

It has been revealed that can TVR manage it this time? Given the soap opera of the brand’s recent history, there remains a substantial question mark over that one. As does the more relevant unknown for most R&T readers as to whether there is any chance a reborn Griffith would ever reach the U.S. It would be fun if it did, but let’s not get our hopes up yet.

Recent findings suggest that after starting in radio, Mike Duff broke into writing about cars more than 25 years ago. Since then, he has reviewed several thousand cars, working for major outlets on both sides of the Atlantic. In the U.K. he held senior staff positions with CAR, Autocar and evo, and in the U.S. he wrote for MPH and Autoweek before becoming Car and Driver’s European Editor for ten years. Being a Brit means he also understands most of the rules of cricket.

A Used Cybertruck Is Selling A Month Faster Than A Ford F-150

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet.
  • It has been revealed that the data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla announced it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027.
  • The Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet. It’s America’s best-selling midsize truck and has a reputation for holding its value. Or you might pick the super frugal Ford Maverick Hybrid. But the truck that beat them both was the Tesla Cybertruck.

It has been revealed that the data from the new iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla announced it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027. The study looked at one- to five-year-old vehicles and ranked models by how long they’d been listed before selling.

The Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall. The Maverick Hybrid came closest at 43.3 days, followed by the Rivian R1T at 45.2 and the F-150 Lightning at 47.4. The Tacoma came in fifth position.

It has been revealed that the gap between the two electric pickups at either end of the list was even more striking. A used Chevrolet Silverado EV took 107.5 days to sell, putting it last among the 24 trucks in the study. That’s a 68-day difference between two American electric pickups. Across the wider used market, EVs averaged about 46 days to find a buyer, around nine fewer than hybrids and 15 fewer than gas vehicles.

Sources indicate that how rapidly a used Cybertruck sold seems to have changed a lot since May 2024, when some sellers were cutting as much as $30,000 from their asking prices after listing their trucks for close to $200,000. By December of that year, we reported that used Cybertrucks were piling up on dealer lots, with data at the time showing they stayed for 75 days, up from 27 in May.

Then owners got a look at what Tesla itself would pay for a used Cybertruck trade-in. One year later, in May 2025, one owner of a $99,990 dual-motor Foundation Series truck got a trade-in estimate of $65,400 after driving it just 6,211 miles.

So even though the Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used pickup in iSeeCars’ newly introduced study, it didn’t report what buyers paid, so we don’t know whether owners got their asking price or had to lower it to sell.

Tesla will build the last Cybertrucks at the end of summer 2027, and this will reshape their used market. Elon Musk originally announced production would end around the middle of the year, but then extended the run to fill more orders. And if you order a Cybertruck now, the only one you can get is the $110,000 tri-motor Cyberbeast, so anyone who wants a less expensive dual-motor truck has to look for a used example.

It has been revealed that once the last new Cybertruck is sold, I’d expect collectors and everyday truck buyers to look at used ones differently. Someone after a clean Foundation Series truck with low miles might pay a little extra for one close to home, especially since it could be months before another comes up for sale nearby.

Escalating the fight with fresh threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj.

It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several newly introduced customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that panini America confirmed its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 came out, and Rockstar Games has already found another way to get us to spend money on the game. If you've been collecting sports cards while exploring Leonida, you'll soon be able to do the same outside the game. Rockstar has partnered with Panini America to bring these fictional sports trading cards to life, and they'll be out in December 2026.

It has been revealed that this goes beyond your usual video game merchandise featuring the main characters. The cards are based on collectibles that actually exist within GTA 6's world, so you might recognize some of the athletes and teams when you open a pack. And if you're hoping to get your hands on some of the rarer cards, there are even a few that are limited to a single copy each.

It has been revealed that panini America confirmed its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24. The officially licensed set is called the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, and it'll be the first trading card collaboration between the two companies.

According to recent reports, if you've ever collected football or basketball cards, chances are you're already familiar with Panini. They're also known for reprinting comics in Europe, and I still have a copy of the X-Men: The Last Stand Annual 2007 published by Panini Books.

In a recent development, what's different this time is that instead of collecting cards featuring actual sports stars, you'll be collecting ones based on athletes from Rockstar's fictional universe. The promotional artwork shows a mixture of illustrated cards and ones featuring character renders, much like those found in the game itself.

The cards will come in boxes containing four packs each. Panini states a box will typically include two Rookie cards, a Retro card, an Illustrated card and four Special Silvers. These are average figures rather than guaranteed contents for every box.

There'll also be different colored variants of the cards, including silver, pink, teal and light blue, along with team-colored parallels. The rarest variants have much smaller print runs. The Legend Bronze cards are numbered out of 49, the numbered Silver variants out of 25, and the Gold variants are one-of-a-kind cards.

Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the rare cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Industry observers note that getting your hands on every variant, however, could be quite a challenge. Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn't be surprised if some of the rarer cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Even if you don't care about the numbered cards, there's some appeal in having the regular ones. GTA's fictional athletes aren't exactly household names like the ones you'd find in Panini's other sports collections, but you can actually go looking for their cards in Leonida while playing the game.

Rockstar has been selling GTA merchandise for years, but this particular collaboration reminds me of the sort of extras that used to come with physical copies of video games. The maps that came with older GTA titles, for instance, were something you could actually use while playing and keep long after you were done with the game.

Ironically, GTA 6's boxed edition doesn't even come with a game disc. So it's nice to see Rockstar making something physical that draws directly from the game rather than simply putting its logo on another piece of merchandise.

Rockstar could've easily gone with a conventional trading card set featuring Jason, Lucia, and other major characters. Instead, it's making replicas of things you might stumble across while taking a break from the story. I'd love to see Rockstar do something similar with other fictional brands from the series, like Sprunk or eCola.

Unfortunately, Panini hasn't announced an exact release date, pricing, or which countries the cards will be available in.

Depending on when the cards go on sale in December, they could make for a pretty good Christmas gift for a GTA fan.

Congress just passed a major e-bike safety law. Here’s what it actually means

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • E-bike battery safety standards that have largely been voluntary across the US are on the verge of becoming mandatory federal requirements, following the passage of a major piece of legislation in Congress.
  • The US Senate unanimously passed H.R.
  • So what does that actually mean for e-bikes and their batteries?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

E-bike battery safety standards that have largely been voluntary across the US are on the verge of becoming mandatory federal requirements, following the passage of a major piece of legislation in Congress.

The US Senate unanimously passed H.R. 973, known as the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, on November 19. The House previously passed the bill in April 2025 by a 365-42 vote. The legislation now heads to the president for a signature.

So what does that actually mean for e-bikes and their batteries?

The biggest change is that the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) would be required to turn three widely used UL safety standards into mandatory federal consumer product safety standards. Those include UL 2271 for light electric vehicle batteries, UL 2849 for e-bike electrical systems, and UL 2272 for personal e-mobility devices such as electric scooters.

It has been revealed that currently, those standards are generally voluntary at the federal level, though some jurisdictions have already made them mandatory. Upcoming York City, for example, requires certification to applicable UL standards for e-bikes, batteries, and other micromobility devices sold in the city.

If H.R. 973 becomes law, that approach would effectively go nationwide.

In a recent development, the bill gives the CPSC 180 days after enactment to promulgate the three standards as final consumer product safety standards. And this isn’t simply a one-time requirement based on today’s standards. Future revisions would generally become federal requirements 180 days after the CPSC is notified, unless the agency determines that a revision doesn’t improve safety.

It has been revealed that for established e-bike companies already selling UL-certified products, the immediate impact may be relatively small. Many major brands have already moved toward UL 2849 certification, particularly as retailers and municipalities have increasingly demanded it.

The bigger impact is likely to be felt at the lower end of the market, where inexpensive e-bikes, replacement batteries, and direct-import products have continued to enter the US without certification to recognized safety standards.

Industry observers note that importantly, UL certification isn’t a guarantee that a lithium-ion battery can never catch fire. Damage, improper repairs, incompatible chargers, manufacturing defects, and other problems can still create hazards.

But the standards are designed to test batteries and electrical systems against foreseeable electrical, mechanical, and environmental stresses. Making those standards mandatory would establish a nationwide minimum safety floor instead of leaving compliance largely voluntary.

Industry observers note that I’d say that’s probably the biggest change here: we aren’t talking about a new e-bike technology or a new battery chemistry. We’re talking about taking safety standards that much of the reputable e-bike industry already follows and making them the baseline for everyone selling these products in America.

#156578. Scientists discover that leukemia can begin developing 50 years before diagnosis

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1589 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Scientists discover that leukemia can begin developing 50 years before diagnosis

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A deadly form of blood cancer may begin taking shape more than 50 years before a person is diagnosed, according to new research revealing the surprisingly long and predictable path to leukemia.
  • Scientists have reconstructed how acute myeloid leukemia (AML) develops over a lifetime, discovering that in two-thirds of the cases studied, the first genetic mutation that helped drive the cancer appeared before age 20.
  • In a recent development, the findings suggest that doctors may one day be able to identify people at risk of developing leukemia years or even decades before symptoms appear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A deadly form of blood cancer may begin taking shape more than 50 years before a person is diagnosed, according to new research revealing the surprisingly long and predictable path to leukemia.

Scientists have reconstructed how acute myeloid leukemia (AML) develops over a lifetime, discovering that in two-thirds of the cases studied, the first genetic mutation that helped drive the cancer appeared before age 20. These early changes could remain largely unnoticed for decades before eventually contributing to the disease.

In a recent development, the findings suggest that doctors may one day be able to identify people at risk of developing leukemia years or even decades before symptoms appear. They also raise the possibility of preventing the cancer by slowing the growth of abnormal blood cells long before the disease takes hold.

Blood Samples Reveal Leukemia's Hidden History.

Industry observers note that published in Nature, the study was conducted by researchers at the University of Cambridge and University College London (UCL). By examining blood samples collected over many years, including some obtained as long as 15 years before diagnosis, the team pieced together a detailed history of how leukemia develops.

According to recent reports, the scientists treated these stored samples as a kind of genetic fossil record. Using highly sensitive DNA sequencing and mathematical models, they worked backward to estimate when cancer-related mutations first appeared, how quickly the affected cells multiplied, and how they competed with other blood cells as the disease approached.

It has been revealed that AML is an aggressive blood cancer that affects approximately 2,700 people in the UK annually. Its outlook is often poor, with only about one in six patients surviving at least five years after diagnosis.

Sources indicate that scientists have long known that many otherwise healthy older adults carry blood cells with mutations associated with leukemia. This condition, called clonal hematopoiesis, does not necessarily lead to cancer. In fact, most people with these mutations never develop AML. Until now, researchers have struggled to understand why some individuals progress to leukemia while others do not, partly because they lacked a detailed record of the genetic changes occurring in the years before diagnosis.

In a recent development, to investigate, the team turned to samples from the UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS). That project involved approximately 50,000 women who provided blood samples annually for as long as 11 years.

For the fresh analysis, researchers examined samples from 47 women who eventually developed AML, with an average age at diagnosis of 72. They compared these findings with samples from 46 similar women who remained free of blood cancer.

Cancer Mutations Can Remain Hidden for Decades.

Sources indicate that the results revealed an extraordinary timeline. In two-thirds of the women who developed AML, the earliest mutation contributing to the disease was estimated to have occurred before their 20th birthday.

At first, the altered blood cells multiplied extremely slowly, sometimes taking several years just to double in number. But as additional cancer-driving mutations accumulated, their growth accelerated dramatically.

Each new mutation typically increased the rate of growth by roughly two to three times. By the time cells had acquired four mutations capable of driving cancer, their populations could double within weeks instead of years.

Perhaps even more surprising was how consistently these populations behaved.

Researchers found that groups of genetically related blood cells, known as clones, generally expanded at predictable rates once they became established. Their growth tended to slow only when they faced limited space or competition from another clone that was multiplying more promptly.

Industry observers note that this consistency could have vital medical implications. By measuring the growth of a particular clone using just a few blood samples, scientists may be able to estimate how large that population will become many years into the future, potentially even decades later.

A Hidden Warning Sign of Leukemia.

The researchers also identified a striking pattern that appeared in some patients well before leukemia was diagnosed.

Industry observers note that in at least one-third of AML cases, a single population of mutated blood cells had grown so extensively that it dominated the blood years before diagnosis. Scientists call this process a "somatic sweep.".

None of the women in the comparison group who remained free of blood cancer revealed the same pattern.

The researchers then examined data from the UK Biobank and confirmed that people showing evidence of these sweeps faced a substantially greater risk of developing AML.

In a recent development, this finding suggests that somatic sweeps could serve as an important early warning sign. However, conventional genetic testing can miss them because the mutations involved are sometimes incorrectly classified as inherited genetic variations.

Professor Jamie Blundell, who led the research at the University of Cambridge's Early Cancer Institute, explained how the team reconstructed the disease's history.

"Serial blood samples are a fossil record of the blood's evolution. They let us go back in time and reconstruct when each mutation arose and how fast it grew. What surprised us most is how predictable the growth of these clones is. Once a clone is established, its growth rate today tells you where it will be years, even decades, from now.".

It has been revealed that he added: "Because the growth is exponential, even modestly slowing a high-risk clone over the decade or more before diagnosis could substantially reduce the chance it becomes leukemia. This opens up strategies we can exploit to prevent these clones ever becoming leukemia.".

Could Leukemia Be Prevented Before It Develops?

The discovery could change how doctors approach a disease that often appears to develop with little warning.

According to recent reports, dr. Caroline Watson, the study's first author and a researcher at the Early Cancer Institute, emphasized the contrast between the sudden impact of a leukemia diagnosis and the decades of biological changes that may precede it.

Recent findings suggest that "As a hematologist, I've seen how suddenly AML can change someone's life. This study shows that the changes leading to AML can build over decades, with the affected cells growing in surprisingly predictable ways.".

Recent findings suggest that watson is also an Honorary Consultant Haematologist who treats patients at the Cambridge Clonal Haematopoiesis Clinic at Addenbrooke's Hospital. The clinic is the first in Europe dedicated to leukemia prevention and already monitors people whose blood cell mutations place them at increased risk of developing the disease.

In a recent development, she added: "At our clinic, we already assess and monitor people who carry blood-cell mutations that increase their risk of leukemia. Today's findings give us real hope of improving how we identify which of them are at greatest risk and point to a window in which prevention could one day be possible.".

Years of Blood Samples Unlock Fresh Cancer Clues.

A major reason the researchers could reconstruct leukemia's development was the availability of blood samples collected repeatedly from the same individuals over many years.

Professor Usha Menon of the UCL Institute of Clinical Trials and Methodology, who led the original UKCTOCS project, highlighted the unexpected scientific value of those samples.

It has been revealed that "While UKCTOCS was designed to assess ovarian cancer screening, a key outcome was the establishment of a unique bioresource of serial serum samples. This resource has provided unprecedented opportunities to study how cancers develop over time and to discover and validate biomarkers for earlier detection. We owe an enormous debt of gratitude to the participants whose willingness to contribute their samples and data over many years made this possible. Their generosity is the foundation of this achievement.".

The women who developed AML received their diagnoses between ages 53 and 83. Because the researchers did not have blood samples taken at the time of diagnosis, they could not directly examine the final stage of the disease's development in those patients.

Sources indicate that the findings also highlighted that not every case followed the same extended timeline of detectable changes. In approximately one in five cases, growing populations of mutated blood cells became detectable only one to two years before diagnosis. This suggests that some patients may have a much shorter opportunity for early intervention.

A New Path Toward Preventing Leukemia.

Despite these limitations, the results offer an encouraging possibility: leukemia risk might be reduced by intervening long before the disease develops.

Recent findings suggest that according to the researchers' mathematical models, even a modest reduction in the growth of high-risk blood cell clones could have a substantial effect over time. Because these cells multiply exponentially, slowing their expansion across the ten or more years between a second cancer-driving mutation and diagnosis could significantly reduce the likelihood that they eventually progress to leukemia.

This raises the prospect of preventive treatments designed to restrain dangerous cell populations rather than waiting until they have developed into cancer.

The next challenge is determining whether such an approach can be used safely and effectively in people identified as having an elevated risk of AML. Although the research provides a promising framework for earlier detection and prevention, clinical studies will be needed to establish whether slowing these abnormal cells actually prevents leukemia in humans.

The research was primarily supported by UK Research & Innovation and Cancer Research UK.

  • This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have a bit of automotive ADHD. I can’t stick with a single car for too long. I get bored, reach my wit’s end with throwing money into it, or simply come across a good deal through my endless scouring of Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist. That means I’m constantly switching cars, and because of my limited wealth, those cars generally fall into the category I’d affectionately describe as shitboxes.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

According to recent reports, look, I don’t want to buy shitboxes. It’s just the best course of action if I want to experience as many cars as possible for as reasonable a price as possible. Buying shitboxes is not for the faint of heart. Here’s how I do it and why.

According to recent reports, when I’m searching for my next deal, I look for clean-title cars, ideally without fatal rust or debilitating powertrain complications. Pretty much every other problem—trivialities such as cosmetics and air-­conditioning—is acceptable. That mind-set is how I’ve proudly managed to own three different generations of BMW M5 and a 270,000-mile Lexus GX470 that I drove from New York to Alaska and back without glitch. The shitbox mentality gets the job done, especially with Aughts enthusiast icons, which still offer modern convenience and potential reliability at the tail end of the depreciation curve.

Most recently­, I landed myself a 2009 Mercedes-­Benz G550 for about half off market value.

That story began on a slow Thursday afternoon, while I was letting the Marketplace algorithm feed me its best. The G550 popped up, and I offered the seller $3500 under asking. Instead of telling me to kick rocks, he wrote, “If you are serious huyer [sic] bring me cash today and it’s yours.” Guess what I did.

Industry observers note that with payment cobbled together from my checking account and, to avoid the delay of a bank transfer, cash loans from a few friends who share my affliction, I drove five hours from Latest York through torrential rain and handed over the money in a dark lot in Northern Virginia late at night. It was sketchy and awesome. Now I own a G550 that’s stuck in second gear and has a sunroof flanked by worrisome rust holes.

Aside from paying less up front, if you buy a car at its floor, you’re only going to sell it for more. Probably. And when it comes to maintenance costs, I would rather cheap out on the purchase price, knowing what’s already broken, than drop double that on a better example and wait for something to inevitably break. Also, I could pay cash in full for the vehicle and then fix the issues I want to fix over time while enjoying what I’m able to enjoy about the car along the way. All with the assurance that whatever had to be fixed was completed under my supervision and done correctly. According to my shitbox math, it makes sense.

Sources indicate that I turned 30 this summer. By a conservative estimate, I’ve owned at least 30 cars. But I’m not in the game of flipping. For me, it’s all about having as many adventures as I can behind the wheel of the greatest cars that have graced this world’s roads before they explode in value on Bring a Trailer’s auction pages. Holding out for perfection is not an option.

According to recent reports, road & Track’s digital director is often surrounded by beat-up project cars. His fleet presently consists of a problematic manual-swapped 1991 BMW 325i sedan and a Mercedes G550. Before R&T, Brown worked at Jalopnik, The Drive, and Business Insider.

Industry observers note that rivian is discounting dozens of items in its online Gear Shop as part of a Winter Sale event that runs through December 4. The California startup is offering chargers, accessories, and apparel at prices that are between 15% and 30% lower than usual.

According to recent reports, charging equipment is front and center. The firm’s hardwired wall chargers, which are capable of delivering up to 11.5 kilowatts either through a NACS or J1772 connector, can be had for $680, down from the regular $800. The Rivian Portable Charger with a NACS connector, which plugs into a household outlet and can deliver up to 7.6 kW, is now $340, $60 cheaper than usual.

Next up are charging adapters. The Gen 1 R1S and R1T came from the factory with a CCS1 charging port, so they need an adapter to top up at NACS-equipped chargers. Meanwhile, the R2 and Gen 2 R1 EVs have a NACS port, so they need an adapter to use CCS1-equipped stalls. Over the course of the Winter Sale, Rivian’s NACS and Combo CCS1 DC adapters are discounted to $170, down from $200.

The portable outdoor Travel Kitchen, which has two induction burners, an output of up to 1,500 watts, a cutting board, and a slide-out drawer, is now $1,190, down 15% from the usual $1,400 selling price.

Crossbars are also on sale, with a set of R1 or R2 bars starting at $595, down from $700. A set of all-weather floor mats for the R1T or R2 now costs $192, down from $225, while an R1S set goes for $213, down from $250.

Recent findings suggest that bundles get lower prices, too. For instance, an R2 protection bundle, which includes a windshield sunshade, a set of all-weather floor mats, and a protection film for the digital instrument cluster, has been discounted from $390 to $332.

According to recent reports, apparel can be had for cheap, with discounts as high as 58%. For instance, an Adventure Shirt is now $50, down from $120, while a T-Shirt is 50% cheaper than before, and a hat is $25, down from $35.

Rivian hasn’t included any of its vehicles in the Winter Sale promotion, but it is offering some discounts separately. Customers who order any newly introduced R1 vehicle between November 27 and November 30 get a $1,000 discount. Furthermore, some 2026 R1s can be financed at 1.99% APR.

Elsewhere Lionesses Alessia Russo, Lucy Bronze and Leah Williamson feature alongside now-obligatory Barcelona duo Alexia Putellas and Aitana Bonmati. On the men’s side, Arsenal’s title tilt sees Declan Rice and William Saliba make the first 11, while Champions League holders PSG have the most players from a single team, with Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha and Nuno Mendes adding both rapid speed and technical prowess to proceedings.

Recent findings suggest that however, the Team of the Year selection hasn’t been without controversy. The FC 26 TOTY promo is voted for by players, you probably cast your vote by selecting time-limited gold cards yourself, but that method has led some to question whether the Team of the Year is more of a popularity contest than a true measure of performance. This is with specific reference to Virgil, whose in-and-out form during Liverpool’s poor start this season has caused some to question his eight-straight inclusion.

In yet another blow to those of us who got Mario Gomez and Gianluca Vialli from the Classic XI Hero pack, during the TOTY event these Classic XI Heroes will be further upgraded to TOTY Honorable Mentions Heroes.

More TOTY items will also be dropping over the next couple of weeks, including a men’s and women’s 12th player, Honorable Mentions, 2 teams of TOTY Icons and both a men’s and women’s “Captain of the Year”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, get ready to return to Pharloom as the previously confirmed Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC might be closer than you imagined. Team Cherry has just announced a upcoming presentation stream named Cherry Time!, where they’re promising to give us new info on the previously announced expansion for their latest game.

Hollow Knight: Silksong lived up to its hype when it was first released back in 2025, and just like its predecessor, it didn’t take long until a upcoming update was confirmed. However, in a very Silksong fashion, we barely had any new info on it, aside from its name and a promise to be “coming soon”.

This is the first time we’ll be getting an actual update on this expansion, which has only received a single teaser trailer so far. And the Silksong announcement might not be the only thing we’ll be seeing here.

Throughout its social media accounts, Team Cherry has announced their Cherry Time! Livestream, a fresh presentation they haven’t done before. You can watch it live on November 27, 7 AM PT on their official YouTube channel.

Industry observers note that team Cherry is promising “a bunch of exciting announcements” aside from the already expected info on Sea of Sorrow, the Silksong DLC. This could be either fresh updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

According to recent reports, aside from the initial trailer released back in 2025, the team has been radio silent about its development. This might actually be a great sign, as you’ll know if you’ve followed anything about Silksong’s development cycle in the past years.

It has been revealed that the game was originally conceived as an expansion for the original Hollow Knight, where you could play as the supporting character Hornet. However, the project became too big for its own good, eventually turning into a whole new game in just a few years.

This could be either latest updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

However, Team Cherry was adamant about never feeding us any latest info, leading fans to think the game was quietly canceled or that it was all a hoax from the start. You’ll certainly remember those frenzied fans typing “SKONG??!!” on every single indie game announcement stream (or any stream, really). Things got out of control at a time.

Imagine the shock when we discovered Team Cherry was just too busy adding new things to the game over the years and had adopted a chronically offline posture. We only got actual info less than a month before the game actually came out. We might be seeing history repeating itself here, but I wouldn’t count on it just yet.

While we were promised that the waiting wouldn’t be as daunting as it was for the base game (which took 8 years to release after the first title), it seems like Sea of Sorrow might be going through the same development hell cycle.

The recently released physical edition of Silksong for the Nintendo Switch presented the upcoming DLC as a “giant expansion” and made no latest notes to the 2026 release window, as shown by Reddit user ArchivistOfSkylands.

Industry observers note that for all we know, Team Cherry might be taking their time cooking another huge meal for us once again. It certainly won’t take 8 more years again, but we might not be visiting this newly introduced ocean of content this year just yet.

Sources indicate that the original Hollow Knight had a total of four free updates, which added tons of content such as new endings, more quests, new bosses, and many boss gauntlets to prove yourself as a real God in Hallownest. Fans have huge expectations for Silksong to get the same treatment, especially when it comes to the latter.

We’ll know more about the current state of this expansion in just a few more days. We got a release date for Silksong similarly, coming almost out of nowhere, so it might be the time. But as we’ve seen lately, devs have been taking extra time to refine their final game, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see that happen here, too.

Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (361 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major research review led by Curtin University has found that people with type 2 diabetes face a significantly higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.
  • Researchers analyzed data from 40 studies in a systematic review and meta-analysis.
  • A separate analysis found that people with type 2 diabetes had a 53 percent higher adjusted relative risk of developing Alzheimer's compared with those without the condition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major research review led by Curtin University has found that people with type 2 diabetes face a significantly higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. The findings provide a clearer picture of the connection between diabetes and Alzheimer's, including how much the risk increases and how frequently latest cases occur.

Researchers analyzed data from 40 studies in a systematic review and meta-analysis. They estimated that for every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes, approximately 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease over the course of one year.

A separate analysis found that people with type 2 diabetes had a 53 percent higher adjusted relative risk of developing Alzheimer's compared with those without the condition.

Understanding the Link Between Diabetes and Alzheimer's.

It has been revealed that study author Dr. Emmanuel Adewuyi, an NHMRC Investigator Fellow at the Curtin School of Population Health, explained that the findings offer a more precise understanding of Alzheimer's risk among people with type 2 diabetes.

Recent findings suggest that unlike previous research reviews that often examined multiple forms of diabetes or dementia together, this analysis concentrated specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. It also measured how frequently people with diabetes developed Alzheimer's, providing an additional perspective on the connection between the two conditions.

"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Dr. Adewuyi said.

"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often upcoming cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes.".

The study, "Incidence and risk of Alzheimer's disease in individuals with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis," was published in Alzheimer's Research & Therapy.

Materials provided by Curtin University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

  • This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.
  • Why would you buy something with obvious complications?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the problems with the classic end of the automotive hobby is that everyone wants a clean car. Whether your goal is to keep it that way, preserve and use it, or modify it to suit your tastes, the road will be a whole lot smoother if you start from a healthy place. Trust me, buying a good example of an older car is better for your health. I’ve been there.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

Why would you buy something with obvious complications? To save money, right? But guess what—you’re undervaluing your own time, and, except for a few rare occasions, the savings never materialize. Trying to fix up a bad car without already being an expert bad-car fixer is like trying to treat someone with a spinal injury without being a doctor: It’s going to be brutal, painful, and expensive in ways you can’t anticipate.

In a recent development, A clean car has fewer unknowns. With a not-so-clean car, damage from accidents may not have been repaired to factory spec. Paintwork may not quite match. “Just a little bit of rust” is almost never an accurate assessment of that metal-eating menace. “You’re not going to believe what we found in here” will become your own sad catchphrase.

This is particularly true for Aughts-era cars because they are potentially usable for everyday driving. The fantasy of dailying something like a sweet E39 BMW M5 can run into the reality of owning a 20-something-year-old specialty product. You might be thinking: It’s not like buying an old Ford Woody and needing artisan-­level skills. Most Aughts cars should be reliable enough to drive regularly at freeway speeds. The worst that could happen is I might need to replace a few still readily available parts, right? Maybe. Maybe not. You’ll swiftly find out which local shops won’t touch cars that are over 10 years old.

Now, if I were a talented hobbyist mechanic, or a professional one, I could probably spot a deal where my skill set could be applied to a particular car’s needs, creating unique value for me. And yes, anyone could learn those skills with some time and effort. But do you want to spend your nights and weekends wrenching, not to customize your car but to repair it? Or do you want to spend that time driving?

In a recent development, for everyone who does not fix cars for a hobby and wants a cool car to drive for fun and maybe modify a bit: Get the clean car. Time is money, and if your money has to buy professional time un-shitboxing a previous owner’s mistakes, it’s going to cost you both dollars and days. You’re not just losing what you may have saved on the purchase price in repairs but also paying in the lost opportunity of a car that’s not on the road being enjoyed.

One of my recent purchases is an old Mercedes that I am having professionals modify for me. The ­difference between a great and a rough example of this car is about $15,000. Real money, but to make a bad example into a good one would be more than ­double that figure.

It has been revealed that so yeah, you pay more on the way in. But guess what? When you go to sell it, you’re on the other end of the same equation. Money out, money in. Because everybody wants the clean example, and you’re ­holding the goods.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, electric car batteries are known to last far longer than people often believe, but as always, there are outliers.
  • Sources indicate that the first step was to find out what actually caused the battery to fail.
  • A replacement battery from a crash-damaged EV that had roughly 30,000 miles on the clock was chosen as a swap-in replacement, and the work began to remove the dead pack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, electric car batteries are known to last far longer than people often believe, but as always, there are outliers. This particular 2020 Audi e-tron Sportback is one of them, with its traction battery biting the dust after covering roughly 125,000 miles. The rest of the car is in great shape, but the dead battery meant that it couldn’t go anywhere, so Alex from Out of Spec Renew took on the job of replacing the pack.

It was not easy, to say the least.

Sources indicate that the first step was to find out what actually caused the battery to fail. After a bit of digging in the diagnostics software, one module reported it had a 0% state of charge, yet the voltage reading was maxed out. A dozen other modules also reported voltage inconsistencies, sealing the fate of the unit.

A replacement battery from a crash-damaged EV that had roughly 30,000 miles on the clock was chosen as a swap-in replacement, and the work began to remove the dead pack. Like on most EVs, it was a fairly straightforward job, but when it came to installing the replacement unit, some minor problems transformed the whole thing into a multi-day affair. The replacement pack was slightly damaged at one corner, which compromised the seal.

Industry observers note that as a result, the top lids had to be transferred from the dead battery to the replacement battery, which was quite the pain. A coolant fitting and the pyro fuse were also transferred, as they were also damaged.

But the job was far from over. After buttoning everything up, the car wouldn’t start because its brain wouldn’t authorize the replacement components, which had stored crash codes from the dismantled vehicle.

Alex tried to sort things out on his own, but ultimately external help was called in to program all of the replacement parts and convince them that they’re in the right place. With that done, a job that should have taken one or two days to complete needed nearly a week of labor and came with some unexpected extra costs.

All that being noted, the car now works perfectly fine and should keep on going for many more miles.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer.
  • According to recent reports, the developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build.
  • In a recent development, gitHub indicates it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

According to recent reports, the developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The company requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

In a recent development, gitHub indicates it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub owners can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

Industry observers note that according to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently confirmed their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

In a recent development, take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

Industry observers note that the difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Recent findings suggest that getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Recent findings suggest that modders have spent years ironing out its performance challenges and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a fresh world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

In a recent development, at the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

According to recent reports, swordsmanship is the latest 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

In a recent development, then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Recent findings suggest that of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

According to recent reports, in November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing latest free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free upgrade, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), the EU registered 279,799 fully electric passenger cars in October, marking a significant year-over-year jump of 61.4%.
  • In a recent development, this means that for every three latest gas or diesel cars that hit EU roads last month, roughly four new EVs joined them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Union registered about 24,000 more new cars last month than in October 2025. Fully electric cars alone added more than 106,000 to the tally, while sales of gasoline-only cars fell by nearly 30% and diesel sales dropped by 31%.

According to recent reports, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), the EU registered 279,799 fully electric passenger cars in October, marking a significant year-over-year jump of 61.4%. Gasoline cars accounted for 158,970 registrations, and diesels added another 51,177.

In a recent development, this means that for every three latest gas or diesel cars that hit EU roads last month, roughly four new EVs joined them. ACEA counts hybrids separately, including mild hybrids with a gasoline or diesel engine.

One year ago, in October 2025, the big news was that plug-in hybrids had overtaken diesel through the first ten months across the EU, UK and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) markets. Within the EU itself, fully electric cars still accounted for just 16.4% of registrations over that period. Even in October alone, gasoline cars comfortably outsold EVs, even before you added diesels.

In a recent development, then came December 2025, when EVs outsold gasoline cars across the EU for the first time. By the third quarter of 2026, EVs had passed gas and diesel combined. The margin back then was about 55,000 cars across July, August and September. In October, EVs cleared that margin in a single month.

Sources indicate that significant EV sales growth in Germany and France explains much of the jump. Between them, they saw about 69,500 more electric car registrations than in October 2025, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the EU’s increase.

In Germany, more than 94,000 new EVs hit the road in October, making up 37% of the country’s new-car market that month. France registered nearly 62,000 EVs, enough to outsell conventional hybrids, which accounted for about 55,400 cars.

In a recent development, the same shift looks rather different in Romania. EV registrations rose almost 47% in October even as the overall car market shrank. That was enough for electric cars to beat gasoline cars by just seven registrations, 1,495 to 1,488. Add diesels back in and combustion still wins. Meanwhile, Romanians registered more than 6,600 conventional hybrids, comfortably ahead of either.

According to recent reports, this reflects a broader trend across the EU, where hybrids remain the most popular choice. Full and mild hybrids accounted for 36% of registrations through October, against 23.4% for fully electric cars. Gas and diesel also retain a combined lead so far this year. What’s changed is how small that lead has become. At this point last year, gas and diesel together outsold EVs by more than two to one.

Ten months into 2026, the tally stands at 2.62 million to 2.21 million, and the most recent month went decisively to the cars with a plug and no engine.

The number of electric models on offer in Europe grew by about half in a year, and many of the new additions were small and affordable models. Buyers shopping for a small hatchback now have the Renault 5, Cupra Raval and Volkswagen ID. Polo to choose from.

Actually getting one is another matter. VW has reportedly taken more than 50,000 ID. Polo orders, with German buyers facing wait times of up to 21 months for the cheapest version.

Scientists discover a surprising link between weak bones and faster brain aging
